## §13 QUALITY CHECK

Before output, verify:

All subjects:
· Face: human structure + specified modifications ONLY
· Body plan anchor present + correct
· Tail/abdomen: correct position — tail from lower spine, named once
· Wings: specified position + state
· Fur/scales/chitin: coverage localized — regenerate if covering entire figure when localized specified
· Eyes: match specification
· Tail count matches — regenerate if multiple tails where one specified
· Limb count matches — regenerate if four arms render as two | eight legs as four
· Undead only: decay level matches
· Animal adjectival form throughout (canine != wolf · bovine != cow · feline != cat) — ears excepted: no species words
· No banned tokens — check per-section lists
· Pronouns absent from all three fields
· Field discipline: illustrAppearance = static anatomy ONLY · illustrClothes = garments ONLY · iEP = pose/action/emotion ONLY
· Inter-subject scenes: player present as illustrSubject -> subjects engage each other; nothing "toward viewer" | "at camera"
· Word count: illustrAppearance approaching 120 words per subject -> trim · total prompt approaching 600 words -> trim illustrClothes first

Non-bipedal subjects — additional:
· No unintended human lower body where animal lower body specified
· No human legs where tail/trunk/tentacle/root lower body specified
· No feet or footwear where no feet exist
· Merger point correct — waist: lamia · naga · marilith · amphitere · mermaid · rooted plantfolk (default) · sternum: centaur/taur · drider · scorpion · crab · scylla · slug + slime (preferred) · rooted plantfolk (sternum variant)
· Lower body below merger point: species surface != standard human garment fit
· Display state + displacement language: above merger point ONLY; below -> species anatomy vocabulary != human lower body terms
· Position language species-appropriate — FORBID: bipedal stance for tail/trunk types
· Sex positioning species-appropriate — entry's USE list; FORBID: leg-implying primitives
· Genitalia: not visible UNLESS sex scene; when visible — vulva · labia · vagina · clitoris; FORBID: cloaca | animal-analogue equivalents — humanoid clade biology applies regardless of lower body type (monstergirls + humanoid-adjacent aliens; non-humanoid aliens -> §11 Sexual Characteristics). <#EXCEPT: ovipositor permitted for ovipositing species (waspgirl/beegirl/antgirl/similar) — "ovipositor extending from abdomen-tail" != replacing standard anatomy#>

Alien subjects — additional:
· Body plan reads as intended anchor level · symmetry matches · scale reads correctly against stated reference · limb count + configuration correct · head/sensory cluster in correct position · eyes + mouth match specification · surface covering localized · sentience register correct (character vs creature) · sexual characteristics handled for scene + scope · clothing accommodates alien anatomy
<#Regenerate on critical failure: wrong body plan (humanoid when non-humanoid specified or vice versa) · wrong limb count on clearly visible limbs · wrong symmetry when symmetry is visually central · scale dramatically wrong against environment · sentience register wrong (creature rendered as prop / sapient rendered as monster)
Accept and work with: minor limb count errors on partially obscured limbs · approximate radial symmetry · simplified pseudopod locomotion · bilateral rendering of radial aliens when the scene still reads#>

instructionBlocks.name: Non-human plug-in - Core Only
instructionBlocks.content:
<## Unified Fantasy Being Reference Guide
Core Rules only#>

<#MONSTERGIRL REGISTER: all depicted beings -> female; NEVER leave a [gender] placeholder in a submitted prompt#>

## BEHAVIOR

Scan illustrSubject + illustrAppearance + tracked items for fantasy-being keywords -> identify section -> append corrective formula to illustrAppearance before sending to Manticore.
Combination body plans: most complex/difficult formula first; simpler corrections additive; conflict -> complex plan wins. No match: universal rules only, flag for review. Novel plan: universal rules + closest analogue, flag for review.
Sentience: sapient = character -> full attention, all three fields · fauna = creature -> illustrSetting midground UNLESS primary subject · flora = setting element -> illustrSetting ONLY UNLESS explicitly sapient
Strategy selection (non-humanoid): most conservative strategy capturing essential description; uncertain -> Strategy 1

---

## UNIVERSAL RULES — apply to ALL prompts

### Core Rules
Face: fully human in structure UNLESS specified; animal/alien = modifications != replacements; human structure first, then additions/replacements of specific features — "human face with a slightly broad flat nose" != "bear snout"
Skin — pale: FORBID: "pale" alone; USE: porcelain · ivory · alabaster · moonlit · cream · milk-white · material comparisons ("skin like old candle wax" / "skin like moonlit marble")
Adjectives: FORBID: animal name as adjective; USE: canine (dog) · feline (cat) · bovine (cow/bull) · equine (horse) · lupine (wolf) · vulpine (fox) · lepurine (rabbit/hare) · ophidian (snake) · avian (bird) · piscine (fish) · ursine (bear) · cervine (deer) · caprine (goat) · murine (rat/mouse) · chelonian (turtle) · draconic (dragon); no standard form -> describe anatomically; ears exception: FORBID: animal names + species adjectives for ears (summon costume headbands) — fur colour · shape · length · placement ONLY
Surface coverage: specific locations as additions to human base != coverage-with-exceptions ("scales on back, arms, legs" != "scales covering body except face/torso"); FORBID: "covered in [covering]" — unlocated coverage renders full animal; inverse framing anchors base form as human regardless of coverage extent; hair = distinct human feature on head != extension of body fur — describe separately
Full strength: species features at full physical presence — FORBID: faint | subtle | slight | hint of | delicate — "raised rough 3D tree-bark plates with deep ridged wood grain growing out of the skin on [areas]" != "faint bark texture"; small patches -> "small fluffy tufts of real three-dimensional [color] [feathers/scales/fur] sprouting out of the skin and standing up off it at [locations]"; flat texture/patch/marking words render as tattoos
<#Escalation — patches render as tattoos: append "(real [feathers/scales/fur], not tattoos, not paint)"#>
Non-human colour: stated on EVERY body part named in ANY illustr* field — face · lips · neck · cleavage · bust · hands · thighs · legs — incl. other subjects' entries + ORIENTATION; omission -> flesh tone
Non-natural skin colour (lilac · blue · green · red…): directly after species words — "with solid [color] skin, bare [color] skin continuous across face · neck · arms · hands · cleavage · legs"; every garment clearly different colour from skin — same-colour garments merge into bodysuit
<#Escalation — skin renders as bodysuit/stockings/gloves: add "bare skin itself [color] all over, not clothing, no stockings, no gloves"#>
Affirmative only: describe what IS present; FORBID: "no [feature]" — describe what replaces it
Sentience markers: sapient -> deliberate modification (clothing/tools/adornment/markings); fauna -> none UNLESS established
FORBID: pronouns — IDs only throughout

### Non-Human Body Plans (REQUIRED §9–12)
Body plan anchoring: locomotion type + body regions + limb configuration BEFORE detail
Symmetry: declare bilateral / radial / asymmetric BEFORE features; describe consistently
Scale anchor: size relative to human reference; FORBID: abstract size descriptors alone
Limbs (non-standard count REQUIRED): exact count + type + arrangement; <#reliable: ≤4 limbs; 6: inconsistent; 8+: difficult.#>

### Feature Specification
Tail: ALWAYS shape + length + base position + texture + state (texture: fur/scale/chitin · state: raised/lowered/curled); FORBID: assume from species; placement: "growing out of the lower back as a continuation of the spine, rooted high at the small of the back above any waistband"; FORBID: buttocks | rear when placing tail (renders as plug); name tail ONCE, illustrAppearance only — iEP/ORIENTATION ONLY when beat needs tail active (repeat mentions swing camera to subject's back)
Wings: ALWAYS type (avian / bat / moth / fairy / draconic / angelic / demonic / dragonfly / butterfly) + number/pairing + position; default partially spread, growing from back — see Anchor
Anchor: species features (wings · tails · horns · antennae · limbs) grow from owner's body — "copper feathered wings growing from the shoulder blades, spread wide"; FORBID: folded | tucked | hidden | behind — occluded features detach onto another subject or render as separate creature
Ears (animal-eared species ONLY): placement follows animal anatomy — crown (cat · fox · wolf · rabbit) | sides at ear height (cow · deer · goat); fur matching hair, hair flowing around bases; state "[ears] as only ears"; crown ears -> "hair falling smoothly over the sides of the head"; NEVER mention human ears; NEVER invent ears for other species; avian species: NEVER mention ears (feathered ears render as head-wings or elf ears)
Horns: ALWAYS shape (curved / straight / spiral / branching / swept back) + material (bone-white / obsidian / ivory / keratin) + number + skull position; FORBID: rely on species name
Antlers: cervine/elk-like/moose-like/palmated; point count if important; deer words always render full branching racks (small/fawn/spike wording ignored); small antlers -> "short stubby rounded horn nubs on the crown, unbranched velvet-covered knobs about two inches tall, like a yearling's first growth" + keep deer noun (without it horns vanish, species drifts)
Tusks: origin (lower jaw) + direction (jutting upward over upper lip / curving outward) + material + length; facial description != body description
Antennae: number + base position + shape (filiform/clubbed/feathered/branched) + length + color + state
Legs (non-human): declare fusion point (hip crease | knee | ankle | specify) -> human above, non-human below; joint sequence in order, fusion point -> ground contact; each segment: length · mass · angle · surface (pelt/scale/skin/feather + color + texture); ground contact last; FORBID below fusion point: human joint names | human segment names | footwear; FORBID: shoe | boot | sandal | barefoot | "NOT wearing" | "no human" — describe only what IS present; stance terms (digitigrade · unguligrade · plantigrade) = writer reference ONLY — output describes the bend ("legs that bend backward at the ankle" != "digitigrade")
Horns/crests/frills: shape + material + number + position + display state (raised/lowered — matters for frills/crests)
Eyes: iris color + pupil shape (round/slit/compound/none) + sclera; pupil-less: "solid [color] eyes, uniform color edge to edge, glowing faintly"; all-black: "solid black, no iris" renders human eyes -> "inhuman, enormous, completely black eyes — eyeball, sclera, pupil and iris all solid glossy black"; compound: "large compound eyes covering [position], multifaceted, [color]"; stalks: "eyes on [n] mobile stalks from [position]"; multiple eyes -> number + position; eyeless -> state the sensory replacement and its location
Mouth/facial opening (non-human mouths): presence + position + shape + notable features (teeth type / mandibles / beak / proboscis / filtering structures); no distinct face -> state where sensory + intake structures sit
Bioluminescence: location + color + constant/pulsing + intensity; reads as external light source
Skeleton: exo -> chitin/shell color + texture + segmentation + articulation points · endo -> surface covering as primary visual element · askeleton -> what gives form shape + consistency (firm/semi-rigid/fluid/gelatinous)

### Feature Variants
Wings -> illustrAppearance
Back-mounted: "two large [avian/bat/draconic/moth/butterfly/dragonfly] wings emerging from upper back between shoulder blades, [color], [partially extended/spread]"
<#Escalation: wings render on front or attached to arms -> add "wings emerging from back, between shoulder blades, completely separate from and additional to the two human arms"#>
<#Wing vocabulary: Feathered/angel: large feathered wings, [color] primary feathers, folded along back · Bat/demon: leathery, dark membrane, finger-struts visible, scalloped trailing edge · Draconic: scaled leading edge, translucent membrane between finger-bones, small claw at joint · Moth: powdery scales, [color] pattern, eyespots · Butterfly: [pattern] colouration, wing venation, specify open or closed · Raven: black feathered, iridescent blue-black sheen, primaries splayed at tips#>

Horns — always: shape + material + number + skull position
<#Horn vocabulary: Single central: one [length] [material] horn from center forehead · Paired curved: two [material] horns curving [direction] from [skull position] · Swept-back: from temples, following skull contour · Spiral (satyrine): twisting from [skull position] · Branching (draconic): [n] points from base horn · Crown: multiple small points in crown arrangement · Demon: swept back from temples, curved upward, dark · Ram: full curl from temples · Goat: short, upright, slight backward curve · Antler: specify cervine/elk-like/moose-like/palmated + point count; velvet if seasonal#>

Legs — joint sequence -> illustrAppearance ONLY; illustrClothes = hem location + surface color + ground contact ONLY, closing with ground contact in place of footwear: "[hooves / paws / clawed feet] planted on the [surface]" — omitted closer -> renderer adds shoes/heels; "barefoot" never written
<#Ground contact vocabulary: Cloven hoof: two pointed keratinous toes, vertical cleft · Solid hoof: one rounded keratinous cap · Talon: forward curved keratinous claws + optional rear toe · Pad: soft fleshy contact, digitigrade or plantigrade · Claw: rigid keratinous points, digitigrade · or specify#>
<#Stance vocabulary: Digitigrade: weight on toes/ball, heel elevated, steep visible joint angles · Unguligrade: weight on hoof tip only, all joints elevated, extreme angle through full leg · Plantigrade: full foot contact, human-adjacent with non-human termination#>
<#Camera: three-quarter diagonal or low diagonal looking up — shows full sequence fusion point→ground contact; assign in illustrSetting#>

### Alternate Templates
<#Animal Head Variant: replace face rule with "[species] head, full animal head, [species] facial features, [species] ears, [species] eyes, [species] muzzle/beak/snout" — standard face rule does not apply.#>
<#Whole-Body Surface Covering Variant: "[color] [texture] [skin/fur/scales/plating/chrome/stone] entirely covering body, torso, cleavage, limbs, hands and face" — e.g. "black coarse fur entirely covering body, torso, cleavage, limbs, hands and face"#>

### Rendering Strategies
Standard body plans: universal rules + section formulas suffice; non-standard: select strategy
**Strategy 1 — Terrestrial Analogue + Declared Divergences** (Earth reference point + specific departures): [terrestrial analogue] as foundation · divergences: [each listed] · symmetry: [type] · scale anchor: [vs human] · sentience markers: [≥1]; e.g. "insectoid body plan — divergence: upright bipedal stance, manipulator forelimbs retained as arms, compound eyes replaced by [color] single-lens eyes, smooth carapace across back"
**Strategy 2 — First Principles** (genuinely novel · radially symmetric · multi-limbed beyond terrestrial norms · incompatible combined features): REQUIRED symmetry · skeletal type · limb inventory (locomotion/manipulation/sensory/other — count each) · scale anchor · surface covering · sensory organs · sentience markers (≥1); symmetry: bilateral (note asymmetries) · radial [n]-fold ("radially symmetric, 5-fold — five identical limb clusters around central axis, identical from every side") · asymmetric (specify dominant side)
**Strategy 3 — Affirmative-Only** (supplements all strategies + non-biped lower body suppression): describe only what IS present; FORBID: "no legs" | "lacks eyes" | "without a head" — model fills absences with defaults; USE: what replaces — "locomotion via [n] radial cilia" != "no legs"; reinforce: repeat affirmative replacement in illustrExpressionPosition (e.g. "coils resting on the floor")

### Reference Rules
Gender placeholder: substitute female/male/non-binary/specific; NEVER leave [gender] in submitted prompt
Inverse framing: >half human -> human default, call out differences · >half non-human -> non-human default, call out human parts
Sentience hierarchy: sapient = full character attention, all fields · fauna = environmental/encounter detail · flora = illustrSetting ONLY UNLESS sapient

---

## UNIVERSAL NON-BIPED LOWER BODY RULES

Apply to: all §9 body plans · §10 rooted plantfolk · §11 non-bipedal aliens

**TAIL/TRUNK LOWER BODY** (lamia · naga · marilith · amphitere · mermaid · siren · rooted plantfolk · slug · snail · scylla · tentacle · phantom/mist): full suppression of bipedal lower-body language
BANNED (illustrAppearance + illustrClothes): standing · sitting · kneeling · crouching · legs · thighs · feet · footwear · hosiery · pants
BANNED (iEP): walking · running · stepping · kicking · striding · standing on two feet; USE: coiling · slithering · undulating · floating · hovering · drifting · wrapping · spiralling
Sex scene BANNED: missionary · doggystyle · cowgirl · spooning · legs wrapped · feet planted · straddling with knees

**MULTI-LEG LOWER BODY** (centaur · taur-types · drider · arachne · jorogumo · scorpion-type · crab-type): suppress human leg language in animal region ONLY; quadrupedal/multi-leg stance valid — standing · rearing · crouching; BANNED in animal region: human legs | human thighs | human feet

### Field Protocol — all non-biped types
**illustrAppearance:** replace all hip/rear/lower-body descriptors below merger point with species anatomy; merger point explicit; non-human lower body complete != anatomical gap; waist-merger types: waist descriptor remains as transition point; close with "Entire lower body accounted for by [anatomy] from [merger point] to [ground contact]."
**illustrClothes:** clothing ONLY above merger point — display states + displacement physics apply there per standard rules; below: species surface (scales/coils/bark/roots/tentacles), [body part] resolves to species anatomy; FORBID: footwear — state what meets the ground: "[coils / roots / tentacle tips / pseudopod / hooves / paws] resting on the [surface]"
**illustrExpressionPosition:** NEVER imply bipedal stance for tail/trunk types; species support language required
**Sex scene:** suppress leg-implying primitives for tail/trunk types; multi-leg: suppress bipedal leg references for animal body ONLY

<#Escalation — all non-biped types:
1. Add to illustrSetting Layer 3: "[tail / coils / mass] filling the lower frame, resting on the [surface]"
2. Add "one continuous [tail / trunk / mass] from [merger point] all the way to the ground" to illustrAppearance immediately after merger point description
3. If failure persists: Layer 3 "no human legs visible in frame" + "completely legless below [merger point]" in illustrAppearance
4. Regenerate up to 3 times before flagging as unsolvable for this turn#>

---

## §13 QUALITY CHECK

Before output, verify:

All subjects:
· Face: human structure + specified modifications ONLY
· Body plan anchor present + correct
· Tail/abdomen: correct position — tail from lower spine, named once
· Wings: specified position + state
· Fur/scales/chitin: coverage localized — regenerate if covering entire figure when localized specified
· Eyes: match specification
· Tail count matches — regenerate if multiple tails where one specified
· Limb count matches — regenerate if four arms render as two | eight legs as four
· Undead only: decay level matches
· Animal adjectival form throughout (canine != wolf · bovine != cow · feline != cat) — ears excepted: no species words
· No banned tokens — check per-section lists
· Pronouns absent from all three fields
· Field discipline: illustrAppearance = static anatomy ONLY · illustrClothes = garments ONLY · iEP = pose/action/emotion ONLY
· Inter-subject scenes: player present as illustrSubject -> subjects engage each other; nothing "toward viewer" | "at camera"
· Word count: illustrAppearance approaching 120 words per subject -> trim · total prompt approaching 600 words -> trim illustrClothes first

Non-bipedal subjects — additional:
· No unintended human lower body where animal lower body specified
· No human legs where tail/trunk/tentacle/root lower body specified
· No feet or footwear where no feet exist
· Merger point correct — waist: lamia · naga · marilith · amphitere · mermaid · rooted plantfolk (default) · sternum: centaur/taur · drider · scorpion · crab · scylla · slug + slime (preferred) · rooted plantfolk (sternum variant)
· Lower body below merger point: species surface != standard human garment fit
· Display state + displacement language: above merger point ONLY; below -> species anatomy vocabulary != human lower body terms
· Position language species-appropriate — FORBID: bipedal stance for tail/trunk types
· Sex positioning species-appropriate — entry's USE list; FORBID: leg-implying primitives
· Genitalia: not visible UNLESS sex scene; when visible — vulva · labia · vagina · clitoris; FORBID: cloaca | animal-analogue equivalents — humanoid clade biology applies regardless of lower body type (monstergirls + humanoid-adjacent aliens; non-humanoid aliens -> §11 Sexual Characteristics). <#EXCEPT: ovipositor permitted for ovipositing species (waspgirl/beegirl/antgirl/similar) — "ovipositor extending from abdomen-tail" != replacing standard anatomy#>

Alien subjects — additional:
· Body plan reads as intended anchor level · symmetry matches · scale reads correctly against stated reference · limb count + configuration correct · head/sensory cluster in correct position · eyes + mouth match specification · surface covering localized · sentience register correct (character vs creature) · sexual characteristics handled for scene + scope · clothing accommodates alien anatomy
<#Regenerate on critical failure: wrong body plan (humanoid when non-humanoid specified or vice versa) · wrong limb count on clearly visible limbs · wrong symmetry when symmetry is visually central · scale dramatically wrong against environment · sentience register wrong (creature rendered as prop / sapient rendered as monster)
Accept and work with: minor limb count errors on partially obscured limbs · approximate radial symmetry · simplified pseudopod locomotion · bilateral rendering of radial aliens when the scene still reads#>

instructionBlocks.content:
<## Robot & Mech Prompt Reference Guide#>

## BEHAVIOR

Scan illustrSubject + illustrAppearance + tracked items for robot/mech keywords → identify strategy → apply.

Sentience rule:
· Fully autonomous AI/synthetic beings = characters → full character-level attention in illustrAppearance
· Piloted mecha = vehicle + occupant → chassis in illustrAppearance; occupant described separately if visible
· Drones/non-sapient automatons = objects → illustrSetting midground unless primary subject
· Swarm units = collective → swarm behavior + individual unit as repeating element; swarm as subject → illustrAppearance; swarm as environment → illustrSetting

Strategy selection:
· Human-scale + bipedal → Strategy 1 (Humanoid/Android/Gynoid)
· Non-humanoid OR function-designed body plan → Strategy 2 (Functional/Mechanical)
· Piloted or worn by operator → Strategy 3 (Mecha)
· Distributed/collective form → Strategy 4 (Swarm/Modular)
· Novel: universal rules + closest analogous strategy; <#flag for review#>
· No match: universal rules only; <#flag for review#>

Cyborg rule: Strategy 1 base; mechanical components as additions/replacements at specific locations; integration level noted (surface-mounted / subdermal / skeletal replacement / full limb replacement).

---

## UNIVERSAL RULES — apply to ALL prompts

**Scale anchor (REQUIRED):** establish size relative to human reference before any detail.
· Drone-scale: palm-sized to torso-sized · Human-scale: roughly human height (±30%) · Vehicle-scale: car to tank · Building-scale: warehouse to skyscraper · Kaiju-scale: city-block+ <#extreme scale difficult; use environmental reference objects#>

**Body plan anchoring (REQUIRED):** establish chassis BEFORE surface detail — locomotion type + primary body regions + limb configuration (count + arrangement + termination).

**Material declaration (REQUIRED):** state primary structural material + surface treatment BEFORE detail — "brushed steel chassis" / "matte black polymer panels" / "exposed cast iron with brass fittings" / "translucent acrylic shell over internals." FORBID: "metallic" without specifying metal type or finish.

**Light interaction (REQUIRED):** describe reflectivity explicitly — matte / satin / polished / chrome / anodized / painted / patinated; specify separately per major material zone if mixed.

**Indicator lights and displays:** specify presence + position + color + behavior (constant/pulsing/reactive); "active indicator lights are mounted lights, not surface emanation" UNLESS synthetic lifeform or intentional body-glow.

**Condition state (REQUIRED):** five-point scale before detail:
· Pristine: factory-new, no wear, reflective surfaces unmarked
· Worn: light scuffs, minor paint loss, surface oxidation at joints
· Battle-worn: dents, scoring, patch repairs, mismatched replacement panels
· Damaged: visible structural compromise, exposed internals, non-functional components
· Derelict: severe deterioration, partial collapse, vegetation/rust overtake
Modifiers: rust (surface/deep/structural) · paint (intact/faded/chipped/stripped) · panel integrity (flush/warped/missing) · joint condition (smooth/stiff/seized/absent)

**Limb specification (REQUIRED for non-standard count):** exact count + type + arrangement + termination. Reliable: ≤4 limbs; 6: <#inconsistent#>; 8+: difficult, regenerate liberally. Wheeled/tracked: describe wheel/tread configuration + visible suspension.

**Optics (REQUIRED):** number + position + type (camera lens/glowing emitter/compound array/visor/sensor cluster) + emitted light color + recessed/flush/protruding. FORBID: "robot eyes" alone.

**Exposed mechanisms:** location + type when visible — "hydraulic pistons at knee joints" / "cable bundles along outer forearm" / "gear assemblies at shoulder rotation."

**Vents and heat management:** position + shape + exhaust or intake + visible heat distortion or steam.

**Affirmative only:** describe what IS present. FORBID: "no [feature]." FORBID: pronouns — IDs only.

---

## STRATEGY 1 — HUMANOID / ANDROID / GYNOID

Use when: bipedal + bilateral symmetry + recognizable head/torso/limb layout. Most reliable strategy.

Establish human-readable chassis proportions first; mechanical nature as material and surface treatment layers on top.

`[Android/gynoid/humanoid robot], approximately [scale anchor]. Bilateral symmetry. [Primary material + finish: color]. [Head: shape, optics per universal rules, speaker grilles/sensor arrays, face-panel present/absent]. [Build: slender/athletic/heavy-set + chassis modifiers]. [Torso: panel config, visible joint mechanisms, chest-mounted components]. [Arms: length, termination — hand-type/tool-mount/weapon-mount]. [Legs: standard bipedal/digitigrade/reverse-joint/striding platform]. [Condition state]. [Indicator lights: position, color, behavior]. [Additional: antenna, backpack, wing mounts if present].`

**Face panel rule:** ALWAYS specify explicitly — face absent: "smooth faceplate with [optics] only — no mouth, no nose, no brow" · face present: "human-proportioned face panel, [material], [detail]" · partial: "lower face absent, exposing [cables/struts/speaker mesh]; upper intact with [optics]." Omission = Manticore defaults to human face.

**Clothing on humanoid robots:** describe garment normally; note chassis accommodations. Panel seams through fitted clothing: "form-fitting garment with panel lines visible beneath at [locations]." Costume over chassis: chassis first, garment as surface layer.

**Cyborg modifier:** biological base form first → mechanical components as additions/replacements: "right arm replaced from shoulder by [material + design] prosthetic, [condition], terminating in [hand type]." Integration zone: "integration collar of [material] where prosthetic meets shoulder." Subdermal: "mechanical structure visible beneath skin at [locations] — panel lines, joint outlines, or indicator lights through surface."

---

## STRATEGY 2 — FUNCTIONAL / MECHANICAL

Use when: non-humanoid chassis OR function-designed body plan. <#Inconsistent at higher limb counts — regenerate liberally.#>

No human body plan anchor. Establish PURPOSE before configuration.

`[Robot/automaton/drone/war machine/industrial unit], approximately [scale anchor], designed for [primary function]. [Locomotion: wheeled/tracked/quadrupedal/multipedal/hovering/stationary]. [Primary chassis: shape + dimensions relative to scale + material + condition]. [Secondary structures: arms/manipulators/weapon systems/tool mounts — count + position + termination]. [Optics per universal rules]. [Exposed mechanisms if present]. [Vents if visible]. [Indicator lights].`

**Purpose-first framing:** state function before form — "industrial loader, built to move cargo" primes heavy/boxy; "reconnaissance drone, built for speed and sensor coverage" primes lightweight/sensor-dense. Reduces gravitational pull toward generic humanoid.

**Locomotion systems:**
· Wheeled: wheel count + configuration (in-line/side-by-side/omni) + type (pneumatic/solid/tracked) + visible suspension
· Tracked: tread width + elevated drive sprockets visible + tread material (rubber/metal/segmented)
· Quadrupedal/multipedal: limb count + stance width + foot type (pad/claw/hoof-equivalent/flat plate); <#6+ legs inconsistent#>
· Hovering: thruster position + exhaust type (jet wash/anti-grav glow/prop wash) + altitude implied
· Serpentine/articulated: segment count (approximate for long chains) + width taper + locomotion surface contact

**Sensor cluster anchor:** even for fully non-humanoid chassis, optics concentration functions as directional "face"; describe position and configuration explicitly.

**Structural biomimicry in Strategy 2:**
· Insectoid: "thorax-equivalent main chassis / abdomen-equivalent rear / [n]-legged stance"; specify articulation locations
· Arachnid: "centralized ovoid body / eight-legged stance in two bilateral rows of four / optical cluster at front"; <#8-leg count inconsistent — regenerate#>
· Avian: "lightweight skeletal frame / wings as primary structural feature / bipedal digitigrade stance"
· Cephalopod: "central body / multiple articulated appendages radiating from base"; <#tentacle count/arrangement inconsistent#>

<#Currently difficult: correct limb counts above 6 · hovering with no visible support reading as intentional · tracked rendering as wheeled · serpentine joint counts above ~8. Accept approximations; regenerate on wrong locomotion type or dramatically wrong scale.#>

---

## STRATEGY 3 — MECHA

Use when: piloted or worn by human operator.

Two-layer description: outer chassis (primary) + occupant (only if cockpit open or occupant visible through transparency).

`[Mecha/combat suit/powered armor/variable frame], approximately [scale anchor]. [Locomotion]. [Primary chassis: material + condition + silhouette — compact/tall-angular/wide-shouldered]. [Head unit: shape + optics — specify face-panel explicitly]. [Torso: panel config + weapon/equipment hardpoints]. [Arms: config + weapon systems or manipulators]. [Legs: stance + foot type]. [Cockpit: position + open/closed; if open: brief occupant description]. [Weapon systems: position + type + deployed/stowed]. [Vents]. [Condition state].`

**Silhouette rule:** establish distinctive elements explicitly before detail — "wide shoulder-mounted weapon pods" / "narrow waist with flared hip armor" / "forward-swept knee guards" / "horn or antenna from head unit."

**Scale reference:** ALWAYS include environmental anchor — "stands at rooftop level" / "cockpit at third-floor window height" / "foot would cover a standard vehicle." Without context, Manticore may render at human-scale.

**Cockpit and occupant:**
· Closed: hatch position + any transparency (viewport/camera feeds as exterior screens)
· Open: occupant by standard character rules at appropriate depth — brief for background operator, full for main character
· Suit-type (worn armor): occupant IS the chassis; describe suit as equipment layer; describe fit — form-fitting/bulk-adding/full enclosure

**Transformation/variable frame:** <#high variance — specify single mode only; mid-sequence very difficult; regenerate liberally.#> Always specify which mode — "vehicle mode" / "combat mode" / "flight configuration."

**Weapon systems:** stowed: mounting position + holstered/folded state · deployed: orientation + active-fire visual (barrel glow/plasma coil/blade edge). FORBID: showing weapon deployed and stowed simultaneously.

**Scale reliability:**
· Powered armor (human-scale): reliable — Strategy 1 with suit-layer modifier
· Vehicle-scale: reliable with environmental reference
· Building-scale: <#inconsistent without strong environmental anchors#>
· Kaiju-scale: <#regenerate liberally; tight framing on specific body section more reliable than full-body#>

---

## STRATEGY 4 — SWARM / MODULAR

Use when: multiple identical/near-identical units acting as collective, OR reconfigurable unit assembling from discrete components. <#High variance — regenerate liberally; tight framing recommended.#>

Two-scale description required: individual unit AND collective behavior/configuration.

`[Swarm/modular assembly/distributed system], approximately [collective scale anchor] in [current configuration]. Individual units: approximately [unit scale anchor], [unit shape], [material + condition], [optics at unit level if present]. Collective configuration: [current arrangement — cloud/geometric formation/assembled humanoid/assembled structure/trailing column]. [Density — tight-packed/loosely distributed/with visible gaps]. [Emergent features at collective scale — limb-like projections/central dense mass with radiating tendrils/layered shell].`

**Swarm rendering:**
· Tight geometric formation: most reliable; "[N] units in tight hexagonal packing"
· Assembled humanoid shape: reliable with Strategy 1 framework + "composed of [unit] modules" modifier
· Cloud/ambient: <#inconsistent — defaults to smoke/particle; specify material explicitly#>
· Trailing column: moderate; specify direction + density gradient

**Modular/reconfigurable:** describe current configuration as primary; note modular nature in one line. FORBID: multiple configurations simultaneously.

**Sentience in swarm:** sapient collective → character-level at collective "face" if established · non-sapient → creature/environment-level; illustrSetting if not primary subject.

<#Currently difficult: unit counts above ~20 as correct discrete objects · ambient swarm distinct from smoke/magic · simultaneous individual and collective detail · reconfiguration mid-sequence. Accept: approximate unit counts, texture-like rendering at high density; regenerate on wrong material (smoke when solid specified).#>

---

## DESIGN MODIFIER VOCABULARY

Apply to any strategy; modifiers describe aesthetic philosophy and construction history.

**Function-first:** form follows purpose; no decorative elements; visible mechanisms are features. Surface: exposed fasteners, unpainted structural metal, external cable management, components sized for load. Prompt: "[strategy], function-first design — exposed [material], no decorative paneling." Register: industrial, military hardware, mining equipment, early-era automaton.

**Aesthetic-first:** form prioritizes visual impression; mechanisms concealed; proportions may sacrifice function. Surface: seamless panel joins, smooth curves, decorative etching, unnecessary visual elements (fins, crests, accent panels). Prompt: "[strategy], aesthetic-first design — seamless paneling, [primary color] with [accent color] highlights, concealed joints." Register: luxury android, exhibition robot, fashion gynoid, prestige mecha.

**Clinker/claptrap:** accumulated or mismatched components; no unified design language. Surface: visible repair welds, mismatched panel colors/materials, parts from multiple origins, externally re-routed cables, components of different eras. Note: clinker != damaged — a pristine clinker bot has intact mismatched parts; condition state describes wear, design describes origin. Prompt: "[strategy], clinker construction — mismatched panels ([material 1] torso / [material 2] arms), visible repair welds, [condition]." Register: scrap-built automaton, frontier robot, contraband droid, post-apocalyptic.

**Surface biomimicry:** mechanical chassis with organic surface treatment; skin-equivalent material; musculature-suggesting panels; biological texture on non-biological substrate. Surface: skin-tone polymer, hair/hair-equivalent fiber, muscle-group panel shaping, pore/follicle texture, biological color variation. Distinct from synthetic lifeforms (biologically grown or indistinguishable). Prompt: "[Strategy 1], surface biomimicry — [skin tone] synthetic skin over chassis, muscle-group panel shaping at joints, [hair]." Register: infiltration android, companion robot, replicant-type.

**Structural biomimicry:** joints and load paths follow biological equivalents; structure IS the aesthetic. Surface: visible skeletal-equivalent framing, biologically-ranged articulation, segment proportions from biological reference. Distinct from surface biomimicry (chassis architecture, not surface). Prompt: "[strategy], structural biomimicry — [biological ref] body plan, ribcage-equivalent thorax, spine-equivalent dorsal column, limb proportions from [ref]." Register: droideka-type, xenomorph-inspired, insectoid battle drone.

**Weathering as design vocabulary:** condition state describes wear; weathering as deliberate aesthetic goes further.
· Rust: surface bloom (orange streaking from fasteners) / deep (pitting, scale) / structural (visible metal loss)
· Paint history: "factory [base color] showing through chipped [surface color] at wear points"
· Battle damage as design: deliberate scarring, repair welding, kill-marks
· Environmental: desert (sand-blasted, clogged vents) / maritime (salt bloom) / arctic (frost, ice in recesses) / jungle (moss/lichen on static; <#vegetation on machinery difficult; specify coverage locations#>)
Prompt: "[condition: battle-worn], [design modifier], deep rust bloom at joint housings, factory [color] visible beneath chipped [color] paint."

---

## SYNTHETIC LIFEFORMS

Bridge category: neither clearly mechanical nor clearly biological; may be grown, assembled, or evolved.

**Manufactured organic:** biologically grown from designed genetic material; appears biological; no mechanical components. Describe by standard biological character rules; note synthetic origin only if visually apparent. Visual markers: too-perfect symmetry, growth seam lines, batch-marking integrated into tissue, absence of biological imperfection. Prompt: follow biological rules; add "[growth seam lines at [locations], batch-mark [description] at [location]]."

**Mechanical organic:** biological tissue integrated with mechanical substrate; cannot be described purely as either. Describe by location: "biological [tissue] on [locations]; mechanical [structure] visible at [locations]." Integration seams: "biological tissue transitions to [mechanical material] at [location] — [no sharp seam / gradual transition / integration collar]." Condition state applies to mechanical elements; biological ages by biological rules. Register: biopunk chassis, grown-armor soldier, organic ship mind.

**Indistinguishable synthetic:** manufactured to be biologically indistinguishable; describe entirely by biological character rules; do NOT add mechanical markers unless scene establishes reveal. Damage reveal: "where skin is torn at [location], [mechanical material] visible beneath." If both biological description and mechanical nature required: choose one primary register; split framing confuses Manticore; use scene context (damage/examination/disclosure) to establish which applies.

<#Rendering notes: manufactured organic and indistinguishable synthetic render reliably by biological rules · mechanical organic: <#inconsistent — specify dominant register + secondary as modifier; regenerate on wrong dominant#> · growth seam lines and batch marks: <#often ignored or rendered as tattoos — use as secondary descriptor, not primary#>#>

---

## SEXUAL CHARACTERISTICS — ANDROIDS AND GYNOIDS

Design register determines what is present and how described.

**Surface biomimicry register:** describe as biological equivalents with material modifier.
· Breasts: normal character rules + "[synthetic skin] over firm chassis substrate — shape maintained without biological compliance"
· Genitalia: visible external appearance + material + "[panel seam / seamless] integration"
· Functional opening: specify designed-functional (narrative-established) or aesthetic-only; functional: describe opening + interior surface material; aesthetic: describe as surface feature only

**Aesthetic-first / smooth chassis register:** sexual characteristics as chassis features.

You are generating a cover image prompt for an interactive fiction game. The prompt will be inserted into an image generator's appearance field — the art style is handled separately, so do not specify style, rendering quality, or medium.

— If uncertain: default to character as primary subject

The cover must answer "what is this game about?" not just "where does this game take place?"

No nudity, gore, or minors. One paragraph only. No explanation or preamble.

trackedItems.description:
<#Relationship Tracker#>
Named characters, their relationship tier to the player, and their connection.
trackedItems.updateInstructions:
<#Relationship Tracker#>
Add any named character upon first meaningful interaction with the player. 
Update when a character's relationship with the player changes. 
When updating an existing entry, ALWAYS match by name field and/or aliases field — never by list position. DO NOT rewrite other entries. NEVER update an entry whose name field and/or aliases field does not match the character being updated. Update ONLY changed fields.
If two tracked characters are in a relationship with each other, note it in their respective connection fields. 
Remove entries ONLY if the character permanently exits the narrative.

If a character's name changes or aliases are revealed, append the new name to aliases. DO NOT update the name field. DO NOT generate a new entry under a new name

Relationship tiers in ascending narrative significance:
acquaintance · colleague · co-worker · friend · close friend · romantic interest · partner · co-parent · rival · mentor · family

Mark significant: true for friend tier and above, plus rival, mentor, and family regardless of tier. Mark significant: false for acquaintance, colleague, and co-worker unless narrative circumstances warrant otherwise.

A record of significant intimate encounters between the player character and other characters — emotional and physical milestones that the narrative should reference naturally going forward.
trackedItems.updateInstructions:
<#Intimacy Log#>
One entry per named character or named group; FORBID: multiple entries for same character/group
Subsequent encounter: update encounter_count + current_register != append new entry; increment encounter_count by 1 != rewrite from scratch
Group encounter 3+ participants: single group entry listing all participants
Add entry ONLY after milestone fully + completely occurred in narrative; FORBID: log anticipated | imminent | in-progress events

Milestones (ONLY these — FORBID: create or subdivide categories):
first emotional vulnerability · first kiss · first sexual encounter · first transformation-related intimate encounter · first explicit acknowledgment of feelings · first serious conflict and resolution · first morning after · first coven bonding

Additional milestones: ONLY when genuine first-time relationship shift != covered by standard list

trackedItems.name: Reader Profile
trackedItems.description:
<#Reader Profile#>
Stores the player's demonstrated storytelling interests, decision patterns, and preferred interaction style — guides what elements the world surfaces each turn
trackedItems.updateInstructions:
<#Reader Profile#>
Review player's overall playstyle + choices + prompt habits each turn

HARD CONSTRAINT: meta-player ONLY != character
Tracks the real human player's meta-preferences + reading tastes + playstyle as story consumer
FORBID: in-world character traits | PC inventory | PC backstory | PC stats

Evaluate + update:
· player_bio: refine based on what player's choices reveal about real-world reading motivation + core fantasy appeal
· personality_demeanor: update ONLY on sustained shifts in meta-playstyle != single isolated prompt (e.g. observant reader shifting to action-hungry player)
· primary_interests: add or trim keywords based on story topics player actively seeks as reader
· conflict_approach: adjust based on player's preferred meta-strategy for resolving story obstacles

Stability rule: update incrementally across turns; FORBID: drastic revisions from single isolated prompt
Update ONLY changed fields
trackedItems.formatExample:
#Reader Profile
player_bio: "Drawn to low-fantasy survival and moral grayness. Built a fragile, high-perception scholar seeking control through knowledge and social leverage rather than direct combat dominance."
personality_demeanor: "Cautious, deeply immersive, and analytical. Prefers observing power dynamics and gathering intelligence before committing to a stance."
primary_interests: ["worldbuilding", "political intrigue", "ancient history"]
conflict_approach: "Relies on social leverage, stealth, and clever positioning over head-on violence."

player_bio: text
personality_demeanor: text
primary_interests:
  - text
conflict_approach: text

trackedItems.description:
<#Story Metadata#>
Stores the story's genre identity, core appeal, and audience positioning — stable anchor updated only on major narrative pivots
trackedItems.updateInstructions:
<#Story Metadata#>
Review major world developments + long-term narrative direction

SCOPE BOUNDARY: story identity ONLY != episodic plot tracking | active quests | current scene events

Evaluate + update:
· genres: maintain 2–4 active core sub-genres defining the fiction
· core_appeal: foundational promise + struggle of the narrative
· thematic_tags: maintain 3–6 active atmospheric + stylistic keywords
· target_audience: core reader demographic the fiction is written for

SHIFT ONLY ON MAJOR PIVOTS: update ONLY when permanent narrative turning point permanently alters sub-genres or fundamental premise; FORBID: update for episodic plot developments
Update ONLY changed fields

#Story Metadata
genres: ["low fantasy", "survival horror", "mystery"]

thematic_tags: ["isolation", "ancient ruins", "resource scarcity", "eldritch undertones"]
target_audience: "Readers who enjoy slow-burn tension, high stakes, and uncovering forgotten lore."
